findings.finding: The zone of proximal development is the range of tasks a learner can perform only with the assistance of a more knowledgeable person.
findings.quote: The zone of proximal development (ZPD) is a concept in educational psychology that represents the space between what a learner is capable of doing unsupported and what the learner cannot do even with support.

findings.finding: Scaffolding involves providing support that is gradually removed as the learner gains mastery.
findings.quote: Scaffolding is a process through which a teacher or a more competent peer helps a student in their ZPD as necessary and tapers off this aid as it becomes unnecessary

findings.finding: Providing the most challenging tasks that a student can manage with support results in the best learning outcomes.
findings.quote: According to Wass and Golding, giving students the hardest tasks they can do with scaffolding leads to the greatest learning gains.

principle: Learning is most effective when a teacher provides support for tasks that a learner can perform with guidance but not yet independently.
for_the_teacher: Offer easier versions of a dance step that the learner can perform with your guidance before attempting the full movement.
Gradually reduce the amount of verbal or visual cues provided as the learner becomes more confident with a specific sequence.
Assess the learner's current ability level to ensure the dance material is challenging but achievable with your support.
